newsitem.title: USA: AT&T unit to securitize $1 bln receivables.
newsitem.headline: AT&T unit to securitize $1 bln receivables.

text.p: AT&T Corp's universal card services unit said it has priced a $1 billion credit card securitization transaction.
The company said the securitization, series 1997-1, consists of two classes of publicly traded floating rate certificates which will be issued by the AT&T universal card master trust.
The company said the senior class, class A, represents $850 million in certificates.
The five-year class A certificates will accrue interest at nine basis points over the three-month London Interbank Offered Rate and were priced at par.
It said $80 million in subordinated five-year class B certificates were also priced at par and will accrue interest at three-month LIBOR plus 28 basis points.
The company said the interest rate on both the class A and class B certificates will be set on May and will reset quarterly.

The company said series 1997-1 also includes a privately funded $70 million collateral invested amount, which will be subordinated to the class A and class B certificates and will provide credit enhancement for the benefit of certificate-holders.

The company said the class A portion of the transaction was managed by an underwriting group led by Lehman Brothers, with Credit Suisse First Boston, J.P. Morgan & Co, Merrill Lynch & Co and Salomon Brothers Inc as co-managers.
The class B portion was managed by Lehman Brothers, with J.P. Morgan & Co as co-manager.

The company said the class A certificates are expected to be rated "AAA" by Standard and Poor's and Fitch, and "Aaa" by Moody's; the class B certificates are expected to be rated "A" by Standard and Poor's and Fitch, and "A2" by Moody's.
